Responsibilities: Position Summary As a Structural Engineering Professional, you will be an integral member of the design team counted on to perform a significant portion of Structural analysis and design for our projects.

You will need strong communication and interpersonal skills as you work closely with your Structural Lead, Structural Engineers, Structural Designers, and other disciplines.

As part of this team, you will help develop design concepts, complete the analysis and design, and work with our Designers to get the structural requirements communicated on design documents and in the model.

It is expected that you have a solid foundation in the fundamentals of Structural Engineering, knowledge of multiple subject areas; experience with US building codes, including seismic provisions; understand how Structural design integrates with and impacts other disciplines; and are building understanding of business trends and industry issues and challenges.

This position may require you to serve as a Lead Structural Engineer for medium-sized projects or as a Sub Lead for larger projects. You will be given as much responsibility as you are willing to take, and your opportunities for career growth will be limited only by your own motivation, capabilities, and attitude. With little or no supervision, competently perform all conventional aspects of Structural Engineering analysis and design

Possess strong knowledge of principles and practices of lateral analysis and design (wind and seismic), including ability to apply required provisions of the building code
Exhibit a high level of attention to detail and quality control
Committed to checking your own work, reaching out to peers and seniors for guidance when questions arise
Perform calculation checking of other engineers' work

Take complete ownership of your portion of the structural scope, reliably working to meet schedule, budget, and quality requirements

Clearly define your own scope and forecast level of effort needed to complete that scope
Be ready to identify scope change and escalate it to your Structural Lead or Project Manager
Recognize when help is needed, reaching out to peers and senior engineers for guidance
Work in a timely, accurate, and cost-effective manner with strong attention to detail
Developing leadership skills
Provide technical guidance, coaching, and/or mentorship to designers/drafters and less experienced engineers
Be proactive in advancing workflows, systems, and tools within the structural discipline; embrace emerging technologies

Project Technical Reviews (40%) Performs Structural Task Leader quality assurance reviews of designs and studies prepared by contractors and in‐house teams to ensure adherence to agency standards and sound engineering principles.

Supports Jurisdictions and Project Management in identifying structural objectives and requirements for inclusion in Statements of Work; reviews and comments on SOWs to ensure discipline‐specific scope and key personnel qualifications are sufficiently identified.

Reviews and provides comments on structural design documents at milestones to identify deficiencies with respect to objectives, requirements, and agency compliance; identifies observable concerns in clarity, completeness, existing conditions, risks, coordination, regulatory compliance, best practices, construction feasibility (phasing/sequence), cost effectiveness, and operational performance.

Provides recommendations at the conclusion of design regarding readiness for bidding and construction. Reviews A/E contractor's proposed variances from agency standards and documents technical positions.

Provides support to resolve design or construction deficiencies, assisting in identification of options and assessing feasibility (constructability, cost, schedule, lifecycle, operations).

Conducts technical reviews of risk and reliability assessments, ensuring consistency with established criteria and professional practices; identifies omissions, discrepancies, and nonconformance and recommends corrective actions.

Technical Advice and Guidance (20%) Assists with project administration and contributes to resolution of technical difficulties amenable to changes in approach and feasibility, risk mitigation, criteria, or requirements; conducts studies to develop criteria for situations encountered during field inspections.

Facilitates resolution of project issues at the Jurisdiction Superintendent level; provides technical guidance on scope, schedule, and budget concerns during programming; delivers timely responses to Jurisdiction representatives and Planning/Project Management divisions; helps prioritize Jurisdiction work.

Coordinates with external parties (e.g., utility companies, departments of transportation, transit authorities, code bodies, historic preservation authorities, and other entities) on projects on or adjacent to agency properties to provide technical representation to ensure structural considerations are addressed to protect government interests.

Structural Engineering Designs and Specifications (15%) Either individually or collaboratively as a project team member, provide supervised assistance to a senior structural engineer with the preparation of structural designs and specifications and performs construction observation to ensure design compliance for a variety of projects. · Participates with customers to develop project requirements and performance criteria. · Conducts site surveys and prepares as‐built drawings of existing conditions in preparation for design. · Analyzes requirements and design criteria; develops cost estimates, validates requirements, and evaluates schedule feasibility.

Project Management (15%) Assists the Project Manager or performs project management duties on assigned projects. Integrates program administration responsibilities related to structural safety, special inspections, and permit/variance tracking into routine project controls.

For contracted studies and designs: · Serves as Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) for assigned structural scope; performs contract administration activities for IDIQ A/E consulting services and specialized procurements. · Prepares Scopes of Work (SOWs), fee estimates, schedules, and solicitation documents prior to award. · Prepares responses to offeror questions, conducts proposal evaluations, and documents award recommendations.

For in‐house studies and designs: · Prepares scope/statement of work; coordinates an integrated team of discipline task leaders; coordinates with the Jurisdiction's project coordinator and other stakeholders. · Manages schedule, budget, and quality; reports status to upper management and meets project requirements.

Program administration: · Assists with administration of structural safety and compliance programs.

Structural Engineering Studies (10%) Provides supervised assistance to a senior structural engineer in the preparation of studies, technical reports, and bulletins that present a range of potential solutions for unique structural problems and challenges.

Completes investigations, field observations, and testing to support the analysis; serves as a technical resource in the execution of testing methods and procedures. Recommends an optimal solution for specific conditions based on professional judgment and documented criteria.

To be creditable, specialized experience must have been equivalent to at least the next lower grade level. Candidates for the GS-12 grade level must have at least 52 weeks of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower (GS-11) grade level.

Candidates for the GS-13 grade level must have at least 52 weeks of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower (GS-12) grade level.

Specialized experience for the GS-13 is defined as having all of the following: Structural engineering experience of complex, monumental, historically significant and mission-critical buildings and building-supporting structures.
